title: Lab 2 - kubectl, Pods and Deployments under pressure
description: Practise the imperative command patterns that save time in the exam, then deliberately break Pods and Deployments and diagnose each failure from its symptoms alone.
scenario:
This lab has two halves. In the first you build things quickly using imperative commands and dry-run scaffolding - the workflow you will actually use in the exam, where writing YAML from memory is far too slow. In the second you break things on purpose: an unschedulable Pod, an image that does not exist, a container that runs out of memory, a rollout that never completes. For each one you diagnose the cause from the symptom before you look at the solution.

Work through it with a timer. Aim to finish the first half in twenty minutes.
environment_setup:
# A two-node cluster is enough for this lab
kind create cluster --name cka-lab2 --config - <<'EOF'
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
nodes:
  - role: control-plane
  - role: worker
EOF

# Set up the shell aliases you should use in every session
alias k=kubectl
export do="--dry-run=client -o yaml"
export now="--force --grace-period=0"

kubectl create namespace lab
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=lab

kubectl get nodes
cleanup:
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=default
kind delete cluster --name cka-lab2

tasks.title: Task 1 - Scaffold a Pod manifest without creating it
tasks.instructions: Generate the YAML for a Pod named 'web' running nginx:1.27 with a container port of 80, write it to web-pod.yaml without creating anything, then add a memory request of 64Mi and a limit of 128Mi and apply it.
tasks.solution:
kubectl run web --image=nginx:1.27 --port=80 --dry-run=client -o yaml > web-pod.yaml

# Edit web-pod.yaml and add under the container:
#   resources:
#     requests:
#       memory: "64Mi"
#     limits:
#       memory: "128Mi"

vim web-pod.yaml
kubectl apply -f web-pod.yaml

# Confirm the resources were applied:
kubectl get pod web -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].resources}'

tasks.title: Task 2 - Imperative Deployment, Service and ConfigMap
tasks.instructions: Without writing any YAML by hand: create a Deployment 'api' with 3 replicas of nginx:1.27, expose it on port 80 as a ClusterIP Service named 'api-svc', and create a ConfigMap 'api-config' with LOG_LEVEL=debug and TIMEOUT=30.
tasks.solution:
kubectl create deployment api --image=nginx:1.27 --replicas=3
kubectl expose deployment api --port=80 --target-port=80 --name=api-svc
kubectl create configmap api-config --from-literal=LOG_LEVEL=debug --from-literal=TIMEOUT=30

# Verify
kubectl get deploy,svc,cm
kubectl get endpoints api-svc
# The endpoints list should contain three Pod IPs.
tasks.verification:
kubectl get endpoints api-svc -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[*].ip}'
# Three IP addresses

tasks.title: Task 3 - Rollout, history and rollback
tasks.instructions: Update the api Deployment to nginx:1.28 with a change-cause annotation. Confirm the rollout completed, inspect the history, then roll back to the previous revision and confirm the image reverted.
tasks.solution:
kubectl set image deployment/api nginx=nginx:1.28
kubectl annotate deployment/api kubernetes.io/change-cause="upgrade to nginx 1.28" --overwrite

kubectl rollout status deployment/api
kubectl get rs -l app=api
# Two ReplicaSets: the new one at 3, the old one at 0

kubectl rollout history deployment/api

kubectl rollout undo deployment/api
kubectl rollout status deployment/api

kubectl get deployment api -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'
# nginx:1.27
tasks.verification:
kubectl get deployment api -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'
# Back to nginx:1.27

tasks.title: Task 4 - Diagnose: a Pod that will not schedule
tasks.instructions: Apply the manifest below. The Pod stays Pending. Before reading the solution, determine why using only kubectl, then fix it so the Pod runs.
tasks.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: picky
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    hardware: gpu
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: nginx:1.27
EOF

# Diagnose
kubectl get pod picky
# STATUS: Pending

kubectl describe pod picky | grep -A5 Events
# Warning FailedScheduling: 0/2 nodes are available:
#   2 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector.

kubectl get nodes --show-labels | grep hardware
# no output - no node carries that label

# Fix: label a node
kubectl label node cka-lab2-worker hardware=gpu
kubectl get pod picky -w   # schedules within seconds
tasks.verification:
kubectl get pod picky -o wide
# Running, with a node assigned

tasks.title: Task 5 - Diagnose: ImagePullBackOff
tasks.instructions: Create a Deployment referencing an image tag that does not exist. Identify the failure from the events, then correct the image and confirm recovery without deleting the Deployment.
tasks.solution:
kubectl create deployment broken-image --image=nginx:1.99-does-not-exist

kubectl get pods -l app=broken-image
# STATUS: ErrImagePull, then ImagePullBackOff

kubectl describe pod -l app=broken-image | grep -A8 Events
# Failed to pull image ...: not found

# Fix in place - no delete required
kubectl set image deployment/broken-image nginx=nginx:1.27
kubectl rollout status deployment/broken-image

tasks.title: Task 6 - Diagnose: CrashLoopBackOff and OOMKilled
tasks.instructions: Create two failing Pods: one whose command exits immediately with an error, and one that allocates more memory than its limit allows. For each, find the exact evidence of what happened - note that the evidence is in a different place for each.
tasks.solution:
# 1. A container that exits non-zero straight away
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: crasher
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox:1.36
      command: ['sh', '-c', 'echo "config file missing" >&2; exit 1']
EOF

kubectl get pod crasher            # CrashLoopBackOff after a few restarts
kubectl logs crasher --previous    # <- the evidence: "config file missing"

# 2. A container that exceeds its memory limit
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: hungry
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: polinux/stress
      command: ['stress']
      args: ['--vm', '1', '--vm-bytes', '250M', '--vm-hang', '1']
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: "100Mi"
        requests:
          memory: "50Mi"
EOF

kubectl get pod hungry
kubectl describe pod hungry | grep -A6 'Last State'
# Last State: Terminated
#   Reason:   OOMKilled
#   Exit Code: 137

# Note: kubectl logs shows nothing useful for the OOM case.
# The kernel killed the process - the evidence is in the Pod status, not the logs.
tasks.verification:
kubectl describe pod hungry | grep OOMKilled
kubectl logs crasher --previous

tasks.title: Task 7 - Diagnose: a rollout that never completes
tasks.instructions: Create a Deployment whose readiness probe can never pass. Observe that the rollout stalls rather than replacing all Pods, explain why the old version is still serving, and then roll back.
tasks.solution:
kubectl create deployment stuck --image=nginx:1.27 --replicas=3
kubectl rollout status deployment/stuck

# Now add a readiness probe pointing at a path that returns 404
kubectl patch deployment stuck --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe",
   "value":{"httpGet":{"path":"/never-ready","port":80},"periodSeconds":5,"failureThreshold":2}}
]'

kubectl rollout status deployment/stuck --timeout=60s
# error: timed out waiting for the condition

kubectl get deploy stuck
# READY 3/3 but UP-TO-DATE 1 -- the rollout stopped after one new Pod

kubectl get pods -l app=stuck
# The new Pod is Running but 0/1 READY

kubectl describe pod -l app=stuck | grep -A5 'Readiness probe failed'

# Why the app is still up: maxUnavailable kept the old ReplicaSet's Pods
# serving because the new Pod never became Ready.
kubectl get rs -l app=stuck

# Roll back
kubectl rollout undo deployment/stuck
kubectl rollout status deployment/stuck
tasks.verification:
kubectl get deployment stuck -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].readinessProbe}'
# empty - the probe is gone after the rollback

tasks.title: Task 8 - Speed drill
tasks.instructions: Time yourself. In under five minutes, and without opening any documentation: create a namespace 'drill'; in it create a Deployment 'cache' with 2 replicas of redis:7-alpine; expose it on port 6379; scale it to 4; label all its Pods tier=data; and write the list of Pod names with their node assignments to /tmp/drill.txt.
tasks.solution:
kubectl create namespace drill

kubectl create deployment cache --image=redis:7-alpine --replicas=2 -n drill
kubectl expose deployment cache --port=6379 --name=cache-svc -n drill
kubectl scale deployment cache --replicas=4 -n drill
kubectl rollout status deployment/cache -n drill

kubectl label pods -l app=cache tier=data -n drill

kubectl get pods -n drill -o custom-columns='NAME:.metadata.name,NODE:.spec.nodeName' \
  --no-headers > /tmp/drill.txt

cat /tmp/drill.txt
tasks.verification:
kubectl get deploy cache -n drill
# READY 4/4
wc -l /tmp/drill.txt
# 4
